---
title: "DataSHIELD analysis scripts"
description: "Drafts tested starter scripts for a DataSHIELD analysis from the analysis plan you write."
---

`datashield-analysis-suggest.yml` is for **analysis projects**, not
packages: projects set up with
[dsAnalysis](https://github.com/nfdi4health/dsAnalysis). You describe
your analysis in a plan file, `config/analysis-plan.yml`: the studies,
the variables and the steps. Each change to that file drafts starter
scripts with the right DataSHIELD calls, **tests them on mock data**, and
proposes them as a [suggestion PR](suggestions.qmd).

::: {.callout-important}
## A starting point, not the analysis
The scripts help you get started with DataSHIELD. They run, but that
doesn't make the analysis right: read and adapt them. The analysis stays
your responsibility.
:::

The plan describes what you want to do before the data is involved, close
to a pre-registration. Claude never sees your data, only the plan.

## How it works

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  subgraph prep ["Prepare"]
    direction LR
    push(["Push that changes<br/>the analysis plan"]) --> check["Check the plan"]
    check --> pkgs["Install the studies'<br/>DataSHIELD packages"]
    pkgs --> mock["Mock data<br/>from the plan"]
  end
  subgraph draft ["For each step, in plan order"]
    direction LR
    claude["Claude drafts the step,<br/>trying its code in DSLite"] --> verify["Check every call,<br/>run the scripts so far in DSLite"]
    verify -- "fails: repair rounds" --> claude
    verify -- "passes" --> next(["Next step"])
  end
  draft --> pr["Suggestion PR"]
  prep --> draft
```

- **The plan is checked first:** all problems are listed at once, before
  anything is installed or sent.
- **The studies' server packages are installed,** at the versions you
  list, together with the matching client packages.
- **Mock data is generated from your variables:** their names, types,
  categories and ranges, so the scripts use your real variable names. Or
  you name your own mock data in the plan (`mock-data`), e.g. made with
  dsAnalysis's `initMockData()`.
- **Claude works as an agent** (Claude Code): for each step it writes the
  code, runs it in DSLite on the mock data together with the scripts
  before it, looks at what comes back and corrects itself, before
  answering. Its sandbox has no network and can't read your login file
  or `.Renviron`.
- **Every DataSHIELD call is checked** against the functions and arguments
  of the installed client packages. Every column has to be a variable of
  your plan or one a step creates. Calls that only look at something
  (`ds.colnames()`, `ds.class()`, …) are sent back, and objects no script
  uses are listed in the report.
- **One step at a time,** in plan order: Claude sees the scripts before
  it and the objects they left on the servers, and the step is tested
  together with them in your project's testing mode (dsAnalysis's DSLite
  setup with the mock data). A failing step gets up to two repair rounds; if it
  still fails, it isn't proposed.
- **A step can run on some studies only** (its `studies` list): every
  call of that step then has to pass those studies as `datasources`.
- **A step waits for the steps it builds on:** by default all steps above
  it, or those named in its `depends_on`. If one of them failed in this
  run, the step isn't written yet; the report says so, and it is tried
  again on the next run.

Details: [analysis plan and checks](datashield-analysis-details.qmd).

## The analysis plan

{{< example analysis-plan.yml config/analysis-plan.yml >}}

The **core** (`symbol`, `studies`, `variables`) is fixed, because the mock
data and the package checks rely on it. The **steps** are free: only a
title is required, and everything else is passed on as you wrote it —
except `depends_on`, which sets what a step builds on. Plans can look
completely different.

## What you get

- **A script per step,** in `R/`: `02_DataManagement.R`,
  `03_DescriptiveStatistics.R`, …, at most 150 lines each. A longer step
  is split between its sections into `02a_…`, `02b_…`.
- **A notes-only script** for a step that isn't possible with your
  studies' packages, saying why and what would be needed.
- **`R/main.R` and `dependencies.R`** each get a marked block that the bot
  maintains: the `source()` lines of its scripts, and the packages to
  install.
- **Mock data** in `utils/mock_data/bot-suggest/` (unless you named your
  own), and your DSLite setup pointed at it. To try the scripts, set
  `R_CONFIG_ACTIVE = 'testing'` in `.Renviron`, restart R and run
  `R/main.R`. That's the same setup the test run used.
- **A report** in the pull request:
  - the tested package versions;
  - steps that would be **possible with another DataSHIELD package**,
    naming the package and its function, with the package's status
    (e.g. production);
  - steps **not possible with any known package**, with a link to an
    existing request for that function, or to open a new one;
  - limitations, and notes on your setup, e.g. credentials written into
    your login file;
  - at the end, a small line saying which model, prompts and settings
    made the scripts.

**Your edits are safe:**
- a script you changed is never overwritten, even when its step changes
  in the plan; the report says so;
- a step removed from the plan keeps its script.

## Before you start

- **The project** must have been set up with dsAnalysis, which provides
  the testing mode and the DSLite setup.
- **Claude access**, one of:
  - **your Claude subscription:** run `claude setup-token` in a terminal
    with [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com) installed, and save the
    token as the repository secret `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Usage counts
    towards your subscription's limits. Only for your own projects: anyone
    who can push to the plan uses your subscription;
  - **an Anthropic organization** through WIF: three secrets and a
    federation rule for this workflow, see [Claude setup](claude-setup.qmd).
- **Pull requests:** either a [GitHub App](getting-started.qmd#github-app)
  or PAT, or the repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
  approve pull requests" (Settings → Actions → General).

::: {.callout-note}
## What leaves your project
The plan's content is sent to Claude: variable names, categories, study
names and the steps. Your data, credentials and your login file
(`R/01_DS_Login.R`) are never sent; the agent's sandbox denies the login
file and `.Renviron`. Don't put anything confidential in the plan.

With a personal subscription (Pro, Max), Anthropic's consumer terms
apply: check the "Help improve Claude" setting in your Claude account
before a real plan goes in.
:::
